title.narrative: Local Currency Initiative for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

description.narrative: The Project aims to increase the access to affordable local currency financing to MSMEs in order to enhance competitiveness and promote business expansion. This would help provide medium- to long-term local currency funding for local businesses and micro-entrepreneurs to strengthen their market position and competitiveness, whilst mitigating their exposure to exchange rate volatility.

title.narrative: Project specific indicators80444

description.narrative: The main impact is expected to be achieved via greater access of the SMEs to medium/long term finance in local currency. Based on the assumption that approximately 15% of the EU Contribution would be allocated to microfinance operations, an assumed EUR 30 million financing to microfinance institutions in local currency would result in approximately 90,000 sustained jobs based on 4 loans provided by the Bank to MFIs. The expected results are highly dependent on the assumptions used (e.g. average loan to the Final Beneficiary of EUR 1,000, the average maturity of the Final Beneficiary loan of 12 months, etc.). Deviations from these assumptions would lead to different outcomes. With indicatively 85% of the EU Contribution allocated to SME operations, EUR 140 million financing to banks in local currency will result in 1,120 SMEs supported, with an average headcount per SME of 15. This would result in 16,800 SME jobs sustained. developed in Ethiopia, Malawi, Tanzania, and Zambia.

The expected results are highly dependent on the assumptions used (e.g. average loan to the Final Beneficiary of EUR 1,000, the average maturity of the Final Beneficiary loan of 12 months, etc.). Deviations from these assumptions would lead to different outcomes. With indicatively 85% of the EU Contribution allocated to SME operations, EUR 140 million financing to banks in local currency will result in 1,120 SMEs supported, with an average headcount per SME of 15. This would result in 16,800 SME jobs sustained.
